name: Python
conventions:
Tests use the standard library `unittest` only (no pytest). The code under test is `solution.py` (plus extra modules if needed) inside starter/, solution/ and every bugs/<name>/. Each test file starts with:

    import os, sys
    sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", os.environ.get("TARGET", "starter")))
    from solution import <names>

Name tests descriptively (`test_last_run_is_kept`): the name is what `bugs[].expect` matches. Use `self.assertEqual(got, want, msg)` with a teaching msg. Type hints on public functions. A starter stub raises `NotImplementedError` or returns a wrong placeholder. Favor idiomatic Python: comprehensions, itertools/collections, generators, dataclasses, exceptions for errors.

levelNotes.5: Good depth topics: generators/iterators protocol, context managers, dataclasses with invariants, functools caching, descriptors.
levelNotes.7: Good depth topics: asyncio ordering and cancellation, heapq/bisect-based structures, memory via __slots__, typing.Protocol.
levelNotes.8: Good depth topics: small interpreters, metaclass-free plugin systems, persistent structures, asyncio schedulers.

image.dockerfile:
FROM python:3.12-slim
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir numpy==2.1.3 pandas==2.2.3 pytest==8.3.3

ecosystem.conventions: numpy 2.1, pandas 2.2 and pytest 8.3 are installed (nothing else). Use them the way a professional would: vectorized numpy/pandas operations instead of Python loops, idiomatic pandas (groupby/agg, merge, pivot_table, resample, rolling, nullable dtypes, explicit sort_values with kind='stable'). Tests use pytest (plain assert, pytest.raises with match=, @pytest.mark.parametrize, tmp_path); test files are tests/test_*.py and load the code under test from ../$TARGET/ exactly as in basics. Compare floats with pytest.approx and DataFrames with pandas.testing.assert_frame_equal. A plausible 'alternative' bug variant is often the pure-Python loop or a pandas call with different semantics (sum vs nansum, nlargest tie order, inner vs left merge, closed/label side of resample).

areas.name: Missing data, dtypes and cleaning in pandas
Time series in pandas (resample, rolling, time zones)
Numerical work with numpy (broadcasting, linear algebra, stability)
